blocks.text: Telecommunications networks create another demanding inventory problem. Copper, fibre and other physical infrastructure run through ducts, cabinets, exchanges and connection points, often with many individual paths sharing the same route. A network inventory has to record more than the street occupied by the cable. It needs enough connectivity and capacity information to relate physical routes to services and planned changes.
